title: Who can open your link: sharing files safely
performance: given a document they need to share from cloud storage, the viewer can choose the narrowest link setting that works, pick view or edit on purpose, say who a forwarded link would reach, and switch access off when the job is done

audience.assumed_prior: knows how to press Share and paste a link; has never looked closely at what each link setting allows
audience.why: the brief says corporate employees who share documents daily and do not know what each setting does
audience.motivation: wants to get a file to colleagues quickly without having to explain a mix-up later
audience.context: watching on a laptop at work or in a short learning slot, with captions, first-language or fluent English

strategy.name: analogy_led
strategy.rationale: the brief's through-line is that a link is a key that travels: the familiar key maps cleanly onto the broad link settings, and the knowledge sheet gives the point where the key stops working (named people checks the account, F12)
strategy.signature_move: Show the key for one setting, say who can walk in, then name the setting; at named people show the door checking the person, not the key.

misconceptions.belief: only the people I send the link to can open it
misconceptions.why_tempting: I sent it to three people, so it feels like a private message

misconceptions.belief: people in the company just means my team
misconceptions.why_tempting: colleagues feel like a small, known group

misconceptions.belief: view only means nobody can take the content
misconceptions.why_tempting: the word view sounds like looking, not keeping

hook.sketch: Imagine you send a budget link to three teammates. A week later, someone you have never met is reading it.

arc.promise: three quick choices before you press Share keep that from happening: who, what they can do, and until when
arc.bridge_from_prior: sec1 starts from the Share link the viewer already pastes into emails and chats every week

sections.goal: the viewer can explain who each of the three link settings lets in, from anyone with the link to named people
the viewer can explain what a person holding the link can do with view and with edit
the viewer can use the three settings to say who a link forwarded once would reach
the viewer can follow the before-sharing checks and the steps that end access

arc.payoff: return to the budget link: the same file goes to the same three teammates, named, view only, switched off afterwards, and nobody else ever opens it

practice_ladder.what: the budget link followed through each setting and one forward, every step narrated
a quiz: three teammates need to read the budget draft, choose the setting and permission
the viewer runs the checks on their own next file before the narrator replays the ending

recall_moments.prompt_sketch: Keep the three doors in mind: anyone, the company, named people. Next we send the link on.
Three teammates need to read the budget draft, not change it: which setting and which permission?
recall_moments.answer: named people, view: the narrowest setting that works, and read-only because they only need to read
recall_moments.tempting_wrong: people in the company, because they are all colleagues: but a forward would then open it for anyone signed in to the company, not just the three

transfer_tasks: the next time you press Share on a real file, ask three questions before you paste the link: who could end up holding this, view or edit, and when will I switch it off

persona.voice: a calm colleague who has seen a link travel too far once, and says so lightly
persona.delivery_notes: even and unhurried; slower and lower on the forwarded link and on named people; brisk and light on the checklist; a short pause before the quiz question

gagne.attention: hook: the budget link read by a stranger
gagne.objective: promise: three choices before you press Share
gagne.recall_prior: bridge: the Share link the viewer pastes every week
gagne.present: sec1 to sec4 in order: who, what they can do, how it travels, how to end it
gagne.guidance: signature move on each setting; key picture then the name
gagne.practice: quiz after sec3; recall_prompt after sec2
gagne.feedback: quiz answer explains why the company setting is the tempting wrong choice
gagne.assess: payoff: the viewer picks setting and permission before the narrator does
gagne.transfer: transfer task: the three questions on the next real file

merrill.problem_centered: the budget link and its three teammates are the running problem
merrill.activation: bridge from the Share link the viewer already uses
merrill.demonstration: sec1 to sec3 show the key at each setting, then one forward
merrill.application: the quiz makes the viewer choose setting and permission
merrill.integration: payoff and transfer task hand the three questions back

mayer.coherence: one document, one forward, no side stories
mayer.signalling: two slowdowns only, on the forward and on named people
mayer.redundancy: screen shows the picture and a few written words; narration explains
mayer.contiguity: each ring, permission and tick appears as it is spoken
mayer.segmenting: four short sections, one idea each
mayer.pre_training: sec1 names the three settings before the forward is traced

arcs.confidence: the key picture before any decision
arcs.satisfaction: the opening link is shared safely at the end
